extraction.name: CADS: A Comprehensive Anatomical Dataset and Segmentation for Whole-Body Anatomy in Computed Tomography
extraction.description: CADS is an open-source framework for whole-body CT segmentation comprising a large-scale dataset of 22,022 CT volumes with complete annotations for 167 anatomical structures. The dataset aggregates diverse CT data from over 40 sources, including public archives, medical challenges, and hospital cohorts, spanning more than 100 imaging facilities across 16 countries. The collection includes both normal and pathological cases across various imaging protocols and patient demographics.

extraction.rai:dataCollection: The CADS-dataset aggregates 22,022 CT volumes from 40 diverse sources including: (1) large-scale public archives including TotalSegmentator (1,203 annotated volumes), National Lung Screening Trial (NLST, 7,172 scans), CT-RATE (3,134 scans), and AbdomenCT-1K (1,062 scans); (2) specialized annotation collections from medical imaging challenges (via Grand Challenge and MICCAI) and focused research studies from The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA); and (3) newly contributed images comprising manual annotations of critical organs-at-risk on the VISCERAL dataset, 484 newly acquired anonymized head CTs from Istanbul Medipol University, and 586 triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CT scans from TUM Klinikum Rechts der Isar. The collection spans data acquired between 2007 and 2024 from over 100 medical centers across 16 countries.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection, Web Scraping, Web API
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: CT scans were collected from multiple sources: public repositories (TotalSegmentator, NLST, CT-RATE, AbdomenCT-1K, TCIA collections), medical imaging challenges (Grand Challenge, MICCAI challenges), and newly acquired hospital data (484 head CTs from Istanbul Medipol University and 586 triphasic contrast-enhanced abdominal CTs from TUM Klinikum Rechts der Isar). The collection includes both healthy subjects and various pathological conditions including oncological diseases (carcinomas, lymphomas, metastases), COVID-19, traumatic injuries, and rare disorders.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: A three-step preprocessing pipeline was implemented: (1) All images were reoriented to the standard RAS (Right-Anterior-Superior) convention; (2) Images were resampled to a uniform 1.5 mm isotropic resolution to balance segmentation accuracy with computational efficiency; (3) Affine transformation matrices were simplified by removing rotation and translation components, preserving only scaling and shear. For patient privacy in newly acquired hospital head CT scans, a Gaussian filter (σ=5 voxels at 1.5 mm spacing) was applied to facial regions to obscure identity while preserving structural integrity. Intensity scaling was performed from the 5th to 95th percentiles to the range [0,1] with clipping for contrast enhancement.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: The annotation methodology employed a multi-stage process: (1) Initial specialized models were trained on high-quality annotations from established datasets for nine anatomical groups; (2) Whole-body pseudo-labeling was performed using these specialized models to propagate annotations across unlabeled scans; (3) Automated outlier detection of pseudo-labels in shape space using neural implicit functions was implemented; (4) Multi-strategy label generation through an ensemble selection mechanism combining three complementary models (GT-flavor trained on original ground truth, Pseudo-flavor using all 22,022 images with pseudo-labels, and Shape-flavor trained on anatomically plausible pseudo-labels after excluding the lowest-scoring 10%); (5) Final label assembly integrated pseudo-labels from the best-performing model flavor for each structure, with original ground truth annotations taking highest priority when available. Structure-specific refinements included rib segmentation correction to preserve costovertebral joints and targeted cropping of head-related pseudo-labels to remove false positives.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: nnU-Net framework (version 2.5.1) with PyTorch (version 2.5.1) and CUDA 12.4
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Performance-driven flavor selection was implemented for each anatomical structure using statistical tests (Shapiro-Wilk test for normality, Levene's test for variance equality, followed by ANOVA, Welch's ANOVA, or Kruskal-Wallis test with post-hoc comparisons). Dice Similarity Coefficient served as the primary metric with 95-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) as secondary metric. Shape-based quality control using neural implicit functions computed anatomical plausibility scores, with the lowest-scoring 10% of images excluded from training. Expert medical review was conducted on 65 test images from TotalSegmentator dataset to identify and correct annotation errors.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: 167 anatomical structures per CT volume in the final CADS-dataset
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three in-house medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist (5.5 years in practice) contributed manual annotations. Expert review for clinical validation was conducted by an experienced radiation oncologist.
extraction.rai:machineAnnotationTools: nnU-Net framework (version 2.5.1), vesselFM foundation model for rib segmentation refinement, ANTS non-rigid transformation for brain structure registration, neural implicit functions for shape-based quality control
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset includes patient CT scans with various demographic characteristics across 16 countries. For newly acquired hospital head CT scans, facial regions were blurred using a Gaussian filter to protect patient identity. The collection includes data from patients aged ≥18 years. Geographic diversity spans multiple continents with data from over 100 medical centers.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset may contain biases related to: (1) Geographic representation with data primarily from specific countries and medical centers; (2) Pathological conditions with higher prevalence of certain oncological diseases in the hospital cohorts; (3) Imaging protocols varying across institutions and time periods; (4) Annotation quality variations between different source datasets, with known systematic errors in structures like ribs and vertebrae in some public datasets that were corrected in CADS. The exclusion strategy in shape-based quality assessment may eliminate cases involving pathological conditions with atypical anatomical variations.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations include: (1) Exclusion of pathological cases with atypical anatomical variations during shape-based quality control; (2) Limited training data for certain structures (e.g., buccal mucosa appears in less than 1,000 scans with only 30 ground-truth annotations); (3) Challenges with very small organs (volumes below 0.5 mL) where standard CT resolution limits and partial volume effects impact accuracy; (4) Anatomically complex structures, particularly small glands, showing lower performance; (5) Brain mask includes all central nervous components within the skull, which may be too inclusive for certain applications; (6) Optic chiasm tends to be under-segmented; (7) Heart segmentation omits superior portions; (8) Rectum appears shorter than anatomical extent; (9) Trachea limited to air content without surrounding tracheal wall; (10) Vena cava needs more precise delineation; (11) Facial features are intentionally anonymized, limiting applications requiring detailed facial analysis.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Dataset use cases include: Training, Testing, Validation, and Fine Tuning of whole-body CT segmentation models. Clinical applications span: (1) Radiation therapy planning through rapid organ delineation; (2) Diagnostic radiology for automated organ volume quantification and detection of anatomical changes; (3) Research applications for large-scale studies across diverse populations and conditions; (4) Anatomical landmark detection for automated measurements; (5) Cross-modality registration for CT-MRI fusion and PET-CT alignment; (6) Anatomy-guided image reconstruction for radiation dose reduction. The dataset is suitable for developing robust AI solutions in radiology and making comprehensive anatomical analysis accessible to clinicians and researchers.
